intro: Legal secretaries manage deadlines, documents and clients precisely, skills that paralegal and compliance work reward. The closest of the 25 careers below is Paralegals and Legal Assistants, with a 92% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $62,890, which is 13% more than the $55,570 legal secretaries earn.
why_it_works: Your days are spent preparing filings, tracking court dates and keeping attorneys and clients organized. O*NET rates time management at 3.25 out of 5 for this job, and service orientation and coordination at 3. Paralegal, court and compliance roles use the same accuracy. Almost all matches need no new degree. The skills to grow are negotiation and managing budgets and materials.
tips: A paralegal certificate is the shortest step up from legal secretary work.
Court Reporters and Simultaneous Captioners earn $72,420, which is 30% more, after training.
Administrative Services Managers earn $114,130, or 105% more, if you manage an office.

faq.q: What jobs can former legal secretaries do?
faq.a: The closest matches are paralegals (92%), government eligibility interviewers (88%) and court, municipal and license clerks (88%), based on O*NET 31.0. Medical Records Specialists are 86% matched and earn $51,140, which is 8% less than the $55,570 legal secretary median.

faq.q: Which careers for legal secretaries pay more?
faq.a: 9 of the 25 matches pay more. Administrative Services Managers earn $114,130 (105% more), Compliance Officers $80,730 (45% more) and court reporters $72,420 (30% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Compliance roles usually need a bachelor's degree.

faq.q: Do legal secretaries need a degree to switch?
faq.a: Usually not. 23 of the 25 matches need no more education than legal secretaries already have, including all of the top 10. A bachelor's degree is common among paralegals, held by 37% of workers, but certificates are also widely accepted.

faq.q: What skills should legal secretaries learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are managing materials, negotiation, managing financial resources and instructing. Coordination already rates 3 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so legal research and office management skills are the main steps up.
